rationale: B wins because it keeps the sharpest finance story as a question instead of pretending the missing underwriting facts are known. B's "Brands get paid on day one. Who carries the 60-day float?" is the right posture; A's "Faire absorbs all the default risk" is a trapdoor because the update never says who funds the float or whether a partner sits behind it. A is usable, but B has better editorial discipline and cleaner refused-angle hygiene.
gaps_in_A: "no bank required" is not in the supplied facts. Faire underwrites using order history, but funding source and banking partners are explicitly unanswered.
"Faire absorbs all the default risk" overstates the record. The facts support a risk question, not a declared risk allocation.
"using purchase frequency and order history" invents a specific underwriting input. The update only gives retailer order history.
"under traditional net-terms arrangements, brands extend credit" imports market context that may be true, but it was not in the update and needs proof before it carries an angle.
gaps_in_B: "cash flow, not demand, decides what they restock" adds a contrast the update does not prove. Cash flow being the top barrier does not establish demand is not a barrier.
"lender" and "loans" may be legally loaded. The update says financing with 60-day payment terms; call it financing until the structure is confirmed.
"category-creation" is the wrong label for the $12.6B strategy angle. The set itself admits this is a single-company story, not category proof.

"A reporter covering late-stage private companies and platform business models at a business or tech-business outlet" is serviceable but still broad. It needs a sharper sub-beat or outlet lane before outreach.
